description.narrative:
The overall objective of the intervention is to enhance partners and other stakeholders abilities to exercise their right to freedom of expression in a responsible, inclusive and diverse manner so that they can provide citizens with reliable public interest content and information (with a specific focus on East-Jerusalem, Area C, and the Gaza Strip).
Under this overarching objective there are three outcomes (pillars):
Outcome 1: Wider media stakeholders/community are encouraged and enabled to produce ethical, inclusive and potentially viable public interest content that audiences trust and civic organisations use.
Outcome 2: Media workers of all genders are better protected online and offline and enjoy safer working environments
Outcome 3: Media support organizations advocate for laws that guarantee freedom of expression and address disinformation and hate speech.

Insatsen ska svara upp mot några av de många utmaningar media och yttrandefriheten står inför i Palestina. International Media Support (IMS) har lämnat in en ansökan till Sida om stöd till IMS Programme Strategy 2022-2024 för Palestina om 36 MSEK (12 MSEK per år 2022-2024). Programmet i Palestina är nära kopplat till IMS Menaprogram (2022-2025) vilket betyder att personal och resurser kan delas i implementeringen. Det föreslagna programmet har bedömts relevant av Sida och insatsen skulle utgöra en fortsättning av ett pågående partnerskap som bygger på tillit och ömsesidig förståelse av en vision att öka ansvarsutkrävande i Palestina över tid, genom ett stärkt civilsamhälle, oberoende media och mer professionella journalister. Insatsen kompletterar andra i portföljen inom mänskliga rättigheter-omårdet, men verkar även kompletterande till det överbryggande stödet till Palestina. IMS huvudsyfte av landstrategin för oPt (Occcupied Palestinian Territory) för 2022-2024 fokuserar på stärkande av partners och andra intressenter/aktörers möjligheter att utöva sin rätt tilll yttrandefrihet på ett ansvarsfullt, inkluderande och diversifierat sätt för att kunna förse medborgarna med påligligt innehåll och information av allmänintresse (med särskilt fokus på östra Jerusalem, område C och Gazaremsan). Under detta övergripande mål finns ett effektmål (impact objective): - Tillgång till innehåll av allmänintresse publiceras av pålitlig media som täcker, sociala, politiska och kulturella ämnen och som verkar för ansvarstagande och ansvarskrävande och människors möjligheter att utöva sina mänskliga rättigheter. Tre resultat: Resultat 1: Större delen av media intressenter/samhället är stärkta och ges möjlighet att producera etiskt, inkluderande och potentiellt livskraftigt innehåll av allmänintresse som publiken litar på och som civilsamhällesorganisationer använder. Resultat 2: Journalisters säkerhet online ökar och deras rättigheter är skyddade i domstol och genom dokumentation av brott mot pressfriheten. Resultat 3: Media stödjer organisationer och civilsamhällesorganisationer lobbar framgångsrikt för lagar som garanerar yttrandefriheten och adresserar desinformation och hatpropaganda.

To respond to some of the many challenges to media and freedom of expression in Palestine. International Media Support (IMS) has submitted a proposal to Sida to fund the IMS programme Strategy 2022-2024 for the Occupied Palestinian Territory with 36 MSEK (12m SEK annually 2022-2024). The Palestine programme is closely linked to the IMS Mena programme (2022-2025) which means it draws on staff and resources for implementation. The proposed programme has been assessed by Sida as relevant and the contribution would be a continuation of an ongoing partnership which is built upon trust and mutual understanding of a long-term vision to enhance accountability in Palestine through an enhanced civil society, independent media and more professional journalists. It is complementary to other contributions in the portfolio within the field of human rights, but also complementary to the overall support to Palestine.
IMS’ main objective of the oPt country strategy for 2022-2024 is focused on enhancing partners’ and other stakeholders’ abilities to exercise their right to freedom of expression in a responsible, inclusive and diverse manner so that they can provide citizens with reliable public interest content and information (with a specific focus on East-Jerusalem, Area C, and the Gaza Strip). Under this overarching objective there is an impact objective: -Access to public interest content published by trusted media which covers social, political and cultural issues and which pushes for accountability and the ability of people to exercise their human rights. and three outcomes: Outcome 1: Wider media stakeholder/community are encouraged and enabled to produce ethical, inclusive and potentially viable public interest content that audiences trust and civic organisations use. Outcome 2: Journalists are safer online and have their rights protected in court and through documentation of press freedom violations. Outcome 3: Media support organizations and CO advocate successfully for laws that guarantee FoE and address disinformation and hate speech.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution International Media Support 2022-2024

description.narrative:
The current agreement period did run from 1 January 2022 through 31 December 2024, being a continuation of a previous agreement period (2018 - 2021). The current achievements have been a continuation of the previous agreement.
During the agreement period, the political and security situation has been highly affecting the implementation of the programme. The events on 7 October 2023 initiated the war on Gaza, which resulted in a escalating repression on the West Bank, and in East Jerusalem. This leading to a widespread digital censorship creating a precarious crisis.
Furthermore, the programme period was affected by the Swedish government imposing a disbursement freeze at the end of October 2023, and initiated a comprehensive review of all aid to Palestine. This suspension, which persisted through the first half of 2024, severely strained the operational capacity for IMS. Also, there was a 16% reduction in funding from Sida in early 2023. This limited both IMS, and their partners, ability to respond to the emerging needs. However, due to the severity on the ground, a temporary and timely, engagement by other donors to IMS were able to mobilize to address the urgent and escalating crisis to some extent.
During the agreement period:
- between 175 and 232 Palestinian journalists have been killed since October 2023. For perspective - this is surpassing the the number of journalists killed in both world wars, Vietnam, Yugoslavia, and Afghanistan combined.
- One partner, Community Development Media Centre (CDMC) in Gaza was entirely displaced.
- Digital repression surged dramatically. This has created an environment where Palestinian stories are systematically erased, or ignored.
Another aspect of the war has been for many organisations to shift their priorities from implementing the planned activities to ensure emergency support being continued for Palestinian journalists in Gaza.
Despite these hurdles, financial but mainly the changed conditions on the ground, IMS has been able to continue their work with their partners, however, with slightly revised activities. This with some results especially worth mentioning, both in general and with regard to the implementing partners:
In general through IMS:
One of the most significant developments has been the expansion of ethical and gender inclusive journalism. This has shown a a growing demand for content that challenges misinformation and exclusionary narratives. There has also been a notable shift towards sustainability measures , including capacity building, funding diversification and strategic networking.
Furthermore, there has been a increasing reliance on digital story telling and multimedia formats. This has been particularly effective in maintaining engagement despite restrictions. In 2024, partners produced over 4 240 content pieces, leveraging innovative techniques to document social and political realities, including the gendered impact on conflict.
In 2024, the programme saw an expansion in partnership, strengthening collaboration with Filastiniyat, CDMC and Wattan TV and introducing Visualizing Palestine (VP). Nisaa FM was faced out, after six years, but they had expanding their funding resources facilitating a diverse reporting, particularly in gender-sensitive content, frontline coverage and digital advocacy.
Also during 2024 there has been a strategic expansion of collaboration with by IMS partners with local, regional and international organisations.
Specific to the implementing partners:
MEDIA Content:
Wattan TV continues supporting citizens journalism, expanding its viewership from 34.9 million in 2021 to 49.9 million in 2024.
Filistiniyat - beyond advocacy, their reports have established direct connections between initiative leaders in Gaza and international donors, securing critical support for vulnerable groups. Many of their reports have been reshaped and amplified by major outlets, such as Al Jazeera and Middle East Monitor.
Furthermore, Filistiniyah received the IPI-IMS Media Award on behalf of Palestinian journalists in Gaza, further enhancing their visibility and advocacy efforts.
CDCM, Community Development Media Centre, offered emergency aid, capacity building and community initiatives to re-build social cohesion. To amplify their findings they launched a social media campaign that reached over 50 000 individuals.
Palestinian platforms have faced growing restrictions, particularly on social media. Despite this Witness interaction among younger audiences and women have grown. Women comprise 55% of social media discussions on Witness' content, while 30% of total call-ins to live shows were from the 18-24 age group - an increase of 20% from the previous year.
Witness focused on storytelling from refugee camps through the "From the Camp" platform. Furthermore, they conducted training for 25 university students on ethical video production and impactful storytelling.
Another important result of the period has been IMS supporting a new initiative, Sabra, aiming at addressing the underrepresentation of Palestinian voices in Israeli, German and global media spaces. Witness, Yura/Untold Palestine and MCC has contributed to this project seeking to reshape public narratives by engaging diverse audiences - particularly Hebrew speakers - who play a key role in shaping the discourse on Palestine.
Safety of Journalists:
During the period there has been a shift from a purely physical and digital security focus to include mental health highlighting a broader understanding of journalists safety that include emotional and psychological wellbeing.
For this reason Filastiniyat has, beyond logistical and financial aid, prioritised the mental health of journalists, including psychosocial counselling sessions as well as handing out sleeping kits, blankets and warm clothing. This as a condition for journalists to be able to continue their work, especially on the West Bank.
They have also conducted extensive research and assessments to understand the evolving challenges faced by many journalists. They have also carried through surveys on evacuated journalists, as well as broader investigative studies on media conditions.
Enabling Environment - Policy & Law.
As a response to the Gaza war, the programme partly shifted from a focus on local law reform to addressing the immediate threats to digital rights and freedom of expression.
IMS partners took an active part in a civil society coalition, led by the UN Office of High Commissioner for Human Rights, that advocated for the cancellation of a draft media law presented by the Palestinian cabinet. The draft contradicted local laws and all international conventions and treaties ratified by the Palestinian Authority in 2014. Widespread opposition led to the Prime Minister freezing the law's implementation, a positive result for media freedom.
In 2024, one of IMS partners, 7amleh, successfully influenced Meta's content moderation policies through advocacy and engagement with the Oversight Board. Key wins included pushing back against restrictive hate speech policies and raising awareness of Meta's approach to Palestinian content.
Unexpected results:
In 2024, while the original plan was to continue offering one-on-one digital security support for selected partners, resource constraints and shifting partner priorities hindered these efforts. Despite the loss of physical infrastructure, efforts were redirected to emergency financial aid and the establishment of temporary safe spaces, including tents for women journalists.
This shift from a purely physical and digital security focus to include mental health highlights a broader understanding of journalist safety that includes emotional and psychological well being.
In general IMS and their partners have been very successful in adapting to the changed conditions on the ground.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
